strategy.summary: Reproduce sympy issue 26821 / PR 26833: Matrix.inv and Matrix.exp over RR[Tau,...] domain produce huge Float coefficients (~1e200-1e251) on the buggy commit c1b1d2d70164; the developer's tests test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 and slow test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 must fail on buggy and pass on fixed revision. Plan: use an editable install from the git checkout at the buggy commit, apply the developer's test diff, run pytest on the selected tests with slow tests enabled.

pinned_because: sympy version unbounded: no documented constraint and no era table entry; strategy chooses to build from the buggy git commit itself rather than a PyPI release, so behaviour matches the revision under test
python_version left null: evidence does not state one; use a Python version supported by that sympy commit (era-inferred, 2024-07)

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit c1b1d2d70164 with the developer test diff applied, test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821 fails because max abs Float in Mi is >= 1e3 (huge floats from RR domain inversion), and test_matrix_exponential_issue_26821 (slow) fails the same way on Me.atoms(Float); on the fixed revision (PR 26833, Matrix.inv converts RR to QQ via exact domain) both tests pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: max(abs(f) for f in Mi.atoms(Float)) for the 7x7 inverse; expected far below 1e3 after fix, around 1e200+ on buggy

input_output_examples.input: 7x7 Matrix with 1.0 entries and symbols Tau, Tau_syn_in, Tau_syn_ex, C_m, Tau_syn_gap times Symbol('__h'); M.inv() then Mi.atoms(Float)
input_output_examples.expected_output: no floats of magnitude around 1e200 or larger; max abs Float < 1e3

input_output_examples.input: M.exp() of the 7x7 matrix with Float 1.0 entries, using t=Symbol('__h') and symbols named Tau, Tau_syn_in, Tau_syn_ex, C_m, Tau_syn_gap; Me.atoms(Float)
input_output_examples.expected_output: Float atoms small, max abs < 1e3 (issue reports {-4.0,-2.0,-1.0,1.0,2.0,4.0} after renaming symbols to aa..ee)

risks: Symbol names affected the original result; the test must keep the names Tau, Tau_syn_in, Tau_syn_ex, C_m, Tau_syn_gap (the matrix-exp test uses symbols('Tau, Tau_syn_in, ...') with names as given) or the bug may not reproduce.
Float coefficients (1.0) are required to trigger the RR domain path; exact-rational input would not transition.
The matrix-exponential test is marked @slow and is skipped unless the --slow flag (sympy's test runner or pytest option) is enabled; running without it would silently not exercise the bug.
Reproduction uses the buggy git commit rather than the 1.13.0 release named in the issue; the numerical transition may depend on the exact commit state of the domain code (gh-25452 regression).

The transition depends on the pure-Python DomainMatrix / polynomial path; if a platform or backend (e.g. gmpy2 availability, which changes Python int/float or rational arithmetic speed but should not change results) differs, behaviour should be checked, though the bug is not expected to be architecture-specific.
No compiler, sanitiser or special architecture is evidenced; the bug is expected to appear on any standard x86_64 Linux build with pure Python.
Not verified: whether the pytest --slow option exists in the chosen checkout; if not, use the sympy bin/test runner with its slow marker support instead.

oracle.tolerance: max abs Float < 1e3 (developer assertion); exact check (M*Mi - eye(7)).applyfunc(cancel) == zeros(7)
oracle.reference_source: developer test assertions in PR 26833 diff
oracle.why: the defect is a magnitude blow-up of float coefficients, so the test asserts a bound on Float magnitude rather than a specific value; the exact cancel check guards correctness of the inverse

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On c1b1d2d70164, Mi.atoms(Float) contains values around 1e200-1e251, so max(abs(f)) < 1e3 is False and the AssertionError fires at the magnitude line in test_inverse_symbolic_float_issue_26821; the matrix-exp test fails the same magnitude assertion on Me.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR 26833 fixed revision, Matrix.inv converts RR[...] to QQ[...] for inversion, so Float atoms are small or absent and both magnitude assertions and the cancel-identity checks pass.
